title: What if one side of Earth never saw night? ☀️
subject: earth
description:
Would you live on the hot side, the cold side, or the twilight strip? 👇

What if Earth became tidally locked to the Sun, turning once per year so one face always points at it? Radio astronomer Alastair Gunn says the day side would get hot enough to boil water while the night side freezes, with violent winds and thunderstorms in between. It would take billions of years and only happen without the Moon, but around the star TRAPPIST-1, all 7 planets are thought to be locked like this already.

Sources: BBC Science Focus, "What would happen if the Earth became tidally locked to the Sun?" (Dr Alastair Gunn, Jodrell Bank Centre for Astrophysics, University of Manchester); CBC Quirks & Quarks, "Will the Earth ever have a dark side?" (Dr Christa Van Laerhoven, University of British Columbia, 2018); NRAO Ask an Astronomer, "What if the Earth became tidally locked to the Sun?" (2022); Wikipedia, "Tidal locking".

scenes.text: Half of Earth would never see the Sun again.
That's if Earth turned once per year, one face locked toward the Sun.
Jodrell Bank astronomer Alastair Gunn says the day side would get hot enough to boil water. The night side would freeze.
The clash would drive violent winds and endless thunderstorms.
Life would cling to a thin twilight strip between them.
It would take billions of years and no Moon. Around TRAPPIST-1, all 7 planets probably live this way already.
